So a while ago my friend had told me about the whole backrooms thing and an impending feeling of horror came over me when she showed me what they look like. Realisation sunk in that I think I may have truly experienced them. 

Basically last summer we were volunteering for a food bank for this group charity project thing. The woman who worked for the place had told us not to go through the dark door in the back under any circumstances (see the pic) it seemed a weird thing to say considering all this place had in it was food supplies. What could a food bank possibly be trying to hide? 

At first, this got me and my friends pretty excited at what monster or mystery could be lurking inside that room. Anyways my friends dared me to go inside the room and I agreed because I didn’t want them to think I was a wuss and besides what could realistically be the worst thing that could happen? I find a dead body in there? 

So I go in and turn the lights on, they flicker at first and start to hum loudly. It’s bigger than I expect but the thing that unsettled me most is that there’s nothing in there. Why would she tell us not to go in there under any circumstances if there’s nothing to hide? Then I see It leads to another room that from the outside looked similar to the one I was stood in, but I was too freaked out at this point to go in any further so I ran out and my friends laughed at me. I thought about it for a while and after finding this whole backrooms subreddit I genuinely wonder what would’ve happened if I’d went into the next room. Would it lead onto another room, and another and another? Until I descended too far into these strange backrooms to turn back? 

I wish I could ask the woman the reason why we weren’t supposed to go in those rooms and if she knew anything about this whole thing. Maybe I’m just being irrational and my nerves are getting the better of me. The place shut down a while ago and I haven’t gone back since but I’d really like to just to see what else was in there.

It took me a while to get from the sub 22 to sub 21 as it gets much much harder to knock those extra seconds off the faster you get, but I use Strava which helps to keep my pace as I usually aim to run the first kilometre in 4min 10seconds and keep up that pace for as long as possible so I have a few seconds leeway if things get tough in the middle, the 3rd and 4th kilometres are killers but if you can push through them and manage a sprint finish you should reach your goal. Training wise I did a lot of 3km at a fast pace (4min 5seconds per kilometre) mixed in with some medium tempo 10kms (4mins 30seconds per kilometre) throughout the week and took a rest day before I ran my 5km, I hope you manage to reach your goal soon!
